A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChartMimic. All 37 pages of v1 and 57 pages of v2, including appendices, provide readable text, tables, equations and figures. The retained tasks and evaluation framework support reliable comparison despite substantial experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 14 models, prompting comparisons, human-evaluation correlations and error analyses in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 17 models, expanded prompting experiments, human-evaluation correlations, judge-stability measurements, split comparisons and additional error analyses.

M1.justification: The chart-generation procedures and four code-traced low-level metrics remain substantively unchanged. SelfRevision becomes SelfReflection with the same substantive prompt (v1 Appendix D; v2 Appendix F). The revisions concern benchmark preparation, evaluated models and scoring settings rather than a new proposed generation algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: Both retain Python-based Direct Mimic and Customized Mimic across 22 chart families. Table 1 expands PIP subcategories from 10 to 20, increasing total subcategories from 191 to 201. Appendix H additionally uses ChartQA and HumanEval performance for auxiliary analysis. Most dataset growth reflects additional examples and augmentation within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 3–4 substantially revise comparator membership: GPT-4o replaces GPT-4V; five InternVL2 and two Qwen2-VL models are added; Qwen-VL-Chat, the two LLaVA-Next-Vicuna models and InternVL-Chat-V1.5 are removed. Several other models, including Phi-3-Vision under its fuller name, remain. Appendix E also adds an empirical CLIP Score comparison.

E3.justification: v1 evaluates 1,000 examples without the later subdivision. v2 constructs 1,200 seed triplets plus three augmentations per seed, divides 4,800 examples into 3,600 test and 1,200 testmini examples, and defaults to testmini. The high-level judge changes from GPT-4V to GPT-4o. Appendix B also revises the reported initial filtering criterion to Matplotlib-generated PDFs; this does not independently establish that construction was rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 expands prompting analysis from GPT-4V alone to GPT-4o and four InternVL2 sizes. New appendices examine test/testmini agreement, judge stability and CLIP comparison, correlations with chart understanding and code generation, and errors in three open-weight models. Prompting and error case studies are revised, including a new successful self-reflection example. The earlier leakage analysis is retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix E.1 newly reports five repetitions of high-level judging, with mean GPT-4o Score 83.4 and standard deviation 0.08. This documents repeated scoring, not additional generation seeds. Pearson coefficients and p-values were already reported in v1; their updated values do not constitute a new statistical practice.

E6.justification: Leaderboards, correlations and error findings are extensively updated. Tables 3–4 report GPT-4V at 71.4/74.9 in v1 and GPT-4o at 81.2/83.2 in v2 under changed data and judging conditions, precluding a same-setting gain claim. Table 5 changes from self-revision underperforming direct prompting for GPT-4V (68.3 versus 71.4) to self-reflection outperforming it for GPT-4o (84.8 versus 81.2). Additional appendix results substantially expand the evidence.

T1.justification: The task equation, low-level F1 construction and CIEDE2000-based color matching remain substantively unchanged. v2 expands standard precision/recall explanations but adds no new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a chart-to-code benchmark with two tasks and multi-level metrics. The abstract updates the claimed resource and evaluation scope, while the introduction newly presents successful self-reflection as evidence for the importance of System 2 reasoning. The headline open-weight performance gap is updated without changing the broader claim that ChartMimic remains challenging.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 moves from explaining unsuccessful alternative prompting on GPT-4V to a model-capability-dependent account of self-reflection, interpreted through System 2 reasoning. Section 4.1 adds an explanation for why customized data may not help difficult charts. Appendix H argues for greater influence from code-generation ability, while Appendices E and K add interpretations about evaluator longevity and extension to other programming environments.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies Python 3.9.0 and Matplotlib 3.8.4, detailed annotation timing and voting criteria, a complexity-assessment rubric, and worked instruction/code examples. Table 9 identifies model checkpoints, API versions and backbones; Appendix E reports judging costs. These substantially improve reproducibility documentation, although many are disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to existing implementations.

R1.justification: v2 adds Plot2Code as closely related chart-to-code work and CharXiv to the benchmark comparison, expanding the discussion of ChartMimic’s distinctiveness through manual curation, diversity and leakage avoidance. It also introduces substantial context from self-correction/System 2 reasoning, CLIP and visualization-recovery research. These changes extend comparative and conceptual positioning beyond citation-style updates.

P1.justification: Although the main section sequence remains, v2 substantially rewrites or expands curation descriptions, metric explanations, prompting discussion and ethics/scalability material. The appendices gain dedicated contributions, split-validation, benchmark-correlation and open-weight-error sections. Terminology changes include SelfRevision to SelfReflection, alongside author, affiliation and publication-header edits.

P2.justification: Table 5 becomes a full-width, multi-model comparison, and Tables 7–9 add split comparisons and model identifiers. New figures illustrate curation, complexity, complete task examples, scoring examples, benchmark correlations and open-weight errors. Existing performance and error displays are revised, while most taxonomy figures are retained and relocated. The conference layout also reflows the document.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation and reproducibility. Compared with v1’s single-model prompting study, it examines five models, checks test/testmini agreement, adds repeated-judge stability and CLIP comparisons, and supplies precise software/model identifiers and curation details. These gains improve confidence in using and interpreting the benchmark. The System 2 and causal interpretations remain stronger than the observational evidence establishes, and changed data/judging prevent direct score comparisons across versions, but the overall methodological documentation and empirical support improve substantially.
